name: PTC 220-222 MHz 25 kHz center-channel overlay

regions: regional except Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas

operator_monitoring_policy.source: Operator-reviewed PTC 220-222 MHz channel-plan workbook, Column G
operator_monitoring_policy.selection_rule: Monitor normal 25 kHz blocks marked Nationwide License, National, or Regional; ignore the 5 kHz allocations and market-specific or unmarked blocks

railfan_01.mode_note: One HR decoder on every requested frequency plus the three packet-observed FR decoders preserves the validated 17-worker resource ceiling while the Pi is thermally capped.

excluded_logical_channels.reason: Column G does not mark these blocks as National/Nationwide or general Regional selections for this deployment.

evidence.source: PTC-220/FRA filing and supplied RF notes

evidence.authority: software-default; not a complete license map

caveats: The supplied notes incorrectly say the center sequence continues to FCC channel 398. Each FCC sub-band has channels 1-200, so the final 25 kHz center is FCC channel 198.

Base/mobile labels describe the conventional paired plan. PTC TDD waivers can permit transmissions in both directions, so transmitter class must be inferred from decoded evidence rather than frequency alone.
The 97-176 overlay defines all possible normal 25 kHz centers; it is not the active receiver selection.
The active selection is the operator-reviewed National/Nationwide and Regional policy above. It is operational scope, not a claim that this file contains a complete regional license map.
